label: sparse copy-phase unit for long (L=9) sequences, favoring inputs 3/o/g/x/z/q
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or on <DEL>), and almost only for long sequences: L=9 holds 85% of activation mass, L=8 14%, L<=6 none. It never fires on the first occurrence of a token, which follows from it being copy-phase only. Within L=9 copy steps it fires on only about 8% of steps. Rates peak at recall_idx 2-3 and at the last two outputs (recall_idx 7-8). The input token matters: 3, o, g, x, z and q have 3-5x lift, and rates also rise with the number of digits in the sequence. (phase==2)&(L>=8) covers 99% of mass but with 5% precision. Adding the token set gives dev F1 0.34 (precision 0.25, mass recall 0.61). Adding position does not get F1 above 0.36. The firing looks diffuse, a sparse function of token and position inside long-sequence copying, and I could not find a clean predicate for it. Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.018) and I did not find what modulates them beyond the token and position lifts.
